ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a bicyclic skeleton in which a benzene ring is fused with a six-membered saturated/unsaturated ring; on the right side of the six-membered ring there is an external positively charged NH2 group, connected to the ring carbon in double-bond form; the lower saturated ring carbon is connected to an O-SO2-NH4/sulfamate-like substituent; several curved arrows and straight arrows are also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: According to the question, ignore all arrows and only transcribe the static connectivity. The heteroatom substituent is written by the specified method as N-O-S(=O)-O, and is connected from the terminal O to the lower saturated ring carbon. The fused bicyclic skeleton is encoded starting from this substituted carbon as C1CC(=[NH2+])Cc2ccccc21, where the benzene ring uses aromatic lowercase c, and the iminium fragment on the right is written as C(=[NH2+]). Connect the substituent with the skeleton, giving the SMILES: NOS(=O)OC1CC(=[NH2+])Cc2ccccc21.

method.method_draft: First transcribe only the static molecular connectivity from the image, ignoring all curved and straight arrows as instructed. Encode the heteroatom substituent as N-O-S(=O)-O attached to the lower saturated ring carbon. Then encode the fused bicyclic carbon skeleton starting at that substituted carbon as C1CC(=[NH2+])Cc2ccccc21, using aromatic lowercase atoms for the benzene part and ring numbers to close the fused system. Concatenate the substituent and fused-ring skeleton to obtain NOS(=O)OC1CC(=[NH2+])Cc2ccccc21.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription is the natural single route for this image-grounded chemistry problem; it uses visual graph extraction rather than any reaction-mechanism inference. Since the task asks to ignore arrows, alternative mechanistic routes would be artificial.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawn molecular graph: a benzene ring fused to a six-membered partially saturated ring; the right upper ring carbon has an exocyclic double bond to positively charged NH2; the lower ring carbon bears an O-sulfur-oxygen-nitrogen substituent shown as OSO2NH4/OSO2NH-type; curved arrows and equilibrium arrow are ignored, while atom labels, charge, bonds, and ring fusion are retained.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to determine the required output format, namely a SMILES expression, and to enforce that arrows in the transition-state drawing should not affect the molecular graph.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply line-angle structure conventions, aromatic benzene SMILES notation, ring-closure numbering for the fused bicyclic system, explicit bracket notation for the positively charged iminium nitrogen as [NH2+], and SMILES valence/connectivity rules for the N-O-S(=O)-O-C sulfamate/sulfinate fragment.
